messages:
maria_ml: Heads up — bringing up hf/hw-llama-2-mod for inference. After 8-bit quant + our conversion, outputs look off compared to HF run. Suspect config.json incompat between rope_scaling, sliding_window and the model's kv/head layout. Anyone seen this combo before?
jonathan: Can you paste the HF config you converted? also which tokenizer/version.
maria_ml: here (raw from the model):
```json
{
  \"architectures\": [\"LlamaForCausalLM\"],
  \"max_position_embeddings\": 4096,
  \"rope_scaling\": {\"type\": \"linear\", \"factor\": 0.5},
  \"sliding_window\": 128,
  \"num_key_value_heads\": 32,
  \"hidden_size\": 8192
}
```
maria_ml: tokenizer has special tokens: {\"bos_token\": \"<s>\", \"eos_token\": \"</s>\", \"pad_token\": \"<pad>\"} — conversion preserved them.
kevin_infra: quick note: our HF->Redwood loader used to map `sliding_window` -> `rw_sliding_window` and default to 2048 when missing. if loader drops sliding_window we end up truncating KV caching at 2048 which will break long-context models.
kevin_infra: also saw rope_scaling handled differently: HF linear scaling factor is applied at runtime by their attention code; our runtime expects a single numeric `rope_alpha` and treats `factor` as a lookup mismatch. leads to mis-scaling of positional rotations.
eva_qa: repro numbers: compared to HF fp16 baseline on the same eval set: F1 down 6pts, perplexity x2 on long-context queries (> 2k tokens), and a few deterministic instruction completions now hallucinate. failing in our regression suite. :face_with_monocle:
jonathan: hmm, num_key_value_heads=32 vs our built-in assumption of heads_per_kv=16 for that hidden_size in the conversion table — that would change KV layout (stride) and quant packing. Could be index offset + garbage read from cache.
maria_ml: interesting — tokenizer alignment might also be off: chat template in model card wraps prompts with `User: ... Assistant:` but our chat template had `</s>` separators which shift pastes and caches.
ci-bot: conversion-smoke-test: hf/hw-llama-2-mod failed `kv-cache-sanity` and `long-context-regression`. logs: `kv_index_out_of_range` in layer 9 during generation.
kevin_infra: suggested quick triage: 1) keep HF `max_position_embeddings=4096` and ensure our loader sets positional truncation limit to that, not default 2048. 2) pass rope_scaling object through the runtime exactly rather than collapsing it — add a compatibility shim mapping linear->rope_alpha calculation. 3) explicit mapping of `num_key_value_heads` -> `kv_heads` in the conversion table, avoid heuristic. 4) ensure chat_template from model card is applied if present.
maria_ml: did a microtest: forced kv_heads=32 at conversion and preserved sliding_window=128 and rope_scaling factor -> our rope_alpha calc, and the worst hallucination case improved significantly. still worse than baseline but much closer.
eva_qa: small quant note — 8-bit packer expects contiguous KV layout; if kv stride mismatches we get misaligned quant blocks which amplify errors after rounding. so fix conversion mapping before re-quant.
jonathan: plan: i'll open a tiny PR to the converter to 1) copy sliding_window verbatim into rw_model.meta, 2) make num_key_value_heads explicit mapping, and 3) add a unit that validates pos_embedding size vs max_position_embeddings.
maria_ml: i'll re-run the 8-bit quant with the fixed converter and attach diff of eval metrics.
kevin_infra: i'll add a canary job: deploy-bot, please run canary with fallback to previous variant if latency/regression exceeds thresholds.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled on eng-dedicated-canary cluster. fallback policy: rollback if QA F1 drops >3 pts or ppl increases >1.5x.
ci-bot: tagging tests to run: `kv-cache-sanity`, `long-context-regression`, `chat-template-compat`, `tokenizer-specials`.
eva_qa: also add a quick smoke that verifies `BOS/EOS` tokens are used consistently between tokenizer and chat template to avoid off-by-one in prefix caching.
maria_ml: thanks all — assigning: jonathan for converter PR, kevin for canary infra, eva for QA runs, me for re-quant + eval. will report back in this thread. :thumbsup:
